geology_unit: Made Ground over Mercia Mudstone Group (Branscombe Mudstone Fm)
land_use: Derelict canal-side brownfield / former industrial land
source_notes: Geology: BGS 1:50k bedrock mapping (Mercia Mudstone Group underlies most of Birmingham Spur, BGS OR/16/034). Fill/made-ground c'-phi' from typical UK made-ground ranges (CIRIA C580 / Hobbs 1998). Drainage capacity assumed low, reflecting Birmingham's largely Victorian-era combined sewer network.

geology_unit: Engineered embankment fill over Sherwood Sandstone Group (Wildmoor Sandstone Fm)
source_notes: Geology: BGS mapping — west Birmingham underlain by Sherwood Sandstone Group (Wikipedia/BGS bedrock 625k; west Birmingham built on Sherwood Sandstone). Steeper slope reflects engineered reservoir embankment geometry. PM low, reflecting greenspace buffering.

geology_unit: Weathered Sherwood Sandstone Group (Wildmoor Sandstone Fm) residual soil
land_use: Major arterial road corridor, high impervious cover
source_notes: Geology per BGS west-Birmingham Sherwood Sandstone outcrop. Air quality: DEFRA UK-AIR 'Birmingham A4540 Roadside' station, recent readings PM10 AQI ~26-30, PM2.5 AQI ~59-80 (aqicn.org, UK-AIR/Defra feed), consistent with DEFRA modelling that Birmingham NO2/PM is up to 50% above legal limits (Birmingham City Council AQMA, UK Authority 2023).

geology_unit: Mercia Mudstone Group (Branscombe Mudstone Fm) with residential made ground
source_notes: Geology per BGS Mercia Mudstone Group mapping (mudstone dominant over sandstone at this horizon). Mixed residential imperviousness (roofs, roads, gardens) taken as C=0.55 (standard hydrology text mid-range value). PM reflects general Birmingham urban background (UK-AIR city-wide AQMA context).

geology_unit: Superficial topsoil/drift over Mercia Mudstone Group
source_notes: Control/low-risk zone. Geology per BGS superficial + Mercia Mudstone bedrock mapping. Air quality reflects DEFRA UK-AIR 'Birmingham Ladywood' station readings on low-pollution days (PM2.5 AQI 15-19 'Good', PM2.5 concentration recorded as low as 3.4 ug/m3, aqicn.org / UK-AIR Defra feed), consistent with vegetative buffering in parkland.
